newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise on housing firm buying frenzy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise on housing firm buying frenzy.

text.p: Blue-chip Medinet Nasr Housing and Development shot to another record high on Thursday, pulling Egyptian share prices up in its wake.

The Capital Market Authority's all-share index rose 0.01 percent to 234.03 points, pushed up by Medinet Nasr which rose 10.00 pounds to a record 185.00 as rumours of a share giveaway at the end of the year fuelled a buying frenzy.
"It may even reach 200 pounds, there is a huge amount of demand but its inching its way up to saturation. It's not a comfortable level," a leading Cairo broker told Reuters.
But Medinet Nasr's runaway success drew investors to other real estate firms and Heliopolis Housing and Development rose 2.10 pounds to 133.75 and Shams Housing and Development gained 0.73 to 13.85.

Brokers said state-owned National Bank of Egypt (NBE) sold part of its stake in joint-venture bank Credit International d'Egypte/CIE to Credit Commercial de France, boosted turnover to a high 59.96 million ($17.6 million).
The National Bank of Egypt -- which owns a total 31 percent stake in CIE -- sold the 82,455 shares for 318.5 pounds each and it was not clear if the sale gave the French bank a majority.
Investors kept up their dynamic trading in the milling firms, described by brokers as the most popular and profitable shares on the bourse.
"It's such a liquid sector and prices are very good for both buyers and sellers. What makes it so attractive is that it works both ways," Mohammed Hossny of Triple A Securities said.

North Cairo Flour Mills -- dubbed "the best stock available" by one trader -- rose 0.25 pounds to 107.50 but other firms ended mixed. Central and West Delta Flour Mills rose 2.16 to 55.16 but Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 0.70 pounds lower at 45.25.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 351.07 points from Wednesday's 352.47 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose again to 164.83 from 164.42 points.
